title: Quaint Flaky British Salmon Quiche
description: A satvik-friendly, fermented, flaky British dish featuring salmon, made in individual mini cocottes and cooked to perfection in a tandoor, perfect for a brunch mood.
instructions: Preheat the tandoor to 375 degrees Fahrenheit.
Roll out the dough on a lightly floured surface to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Cut out four 6-inch squares of dough and press each into a mini cocotte.
Divide the salmon into four equal pieces and place one piece in each cocotte.
In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, heavy cream, dried dill weed, salt, and black pepper.
Pour the egg mixture over the salmon in each cocotte.
Roll out the remaining dough to a thickness of about 1/8 inch and cut into four 6-inch squares.
Use the remaining dough squares to cover each cocotte and press the edges to seal.
Brush the tops of the quiches with a little water and cut a few slits in the top of each to allow steam to escape.
Place the quiches in the preheated tandoor and bake for 25 minutes.
Reduce the heat to 350 degrees Fahrenheit and continue baking for an additional 10 minutes.
